metadata.case_name: WONG HIN PUI v. MOK YING KIT AND ANOTHER

source: He had sustained a serious injury to his head which ought to have been apparent to those at the Tai Po clinic who had kept him waiting and then sent him home.

injuries.description: haematomas which had built up within his skull (evacuated)
source: He had two operations carried out on his head including evacuation of haematomas which had built up within his skull.

His left sided hemiparesis affects his arms particularly severely. When the left hand grips, he needs to lever it open to release that grip. He can use it to a limited extent to steady or support an object providing that not much weight is involved. It has no capacity for fine movements.
and epileptiform attacks requiring anti-convulsant treatment.
He has regular epileptiform seizures or convulsions which are focal in nature.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

source: There is also a significant cognitive deficit as attested to by Professor Peter Lee

injuries.description: significant cosmetic defect (external result of earlier surgery)
source: He is nonetheless left with a significant cosmetic defect of which he tries to make light as much as he can

injuries.description: post-concussional disorder (syndrome) and Dysthymic disorders / depressive disorder
source: Dr Chung diagnosed the Plaintiff as suffering from post-concussional disorder (or syndrome) and Dysthymic disorders in April 1998. He expected his condition to be permanent with a need for long term psychiatric support.
Dr Singer saw the Plaintiff in May 1999. He diagnosed a depressive disorder and post-concussional syndrome.

manifestations.description: unable to respond to any verbal contact for a further week after intensive care
left sided hemiparesis with severe arm involvement; inability to perform fine movements; requires levering to release grip
regular epileptiform seizures or convulsions, focal in nature; reduced frequency in recent months; on anti-convulsant medication
significant cosmetic defect as a result of earlier surgery
post-concussional disorder / dysthymic / depressive disorder with need for psychiatric/psychotherapeutic support

treatments_received: two operations on head including evacuation of intracranial haematomas
cranioplasty about one year after discharge from convalescent hospital
treatments_future: physiotherapy monitoring and use of exercise machine

losses.description: General pain, suffering and loss of amenity including permanent neurological deficits and functional impairment
Significant cosmetic defect following head injury and surgery
Reduced ability to live independently; need for domestic help and alternative accommodation
Disruption and loss of family life including disappearance of his wife with his son, rejection by family and loss of home and employment
Unemployable on the open market as a consequence of his injuries
